candidates.name: git-fetch documentation
verified_facts: git fetch downloads objects and refs needed from the remote repository
Fetched remote-tracking refs can be read back before applying a local update
semantic_limits: Fetch alone does not modify the checked-out working tree or prove that the external F-host daemon is running

candidates.name: git-pull documentation
verified_facts: The --ff-only option refuses an update when the local and remote histories have diverged
Pull combines fetch with integration of the selected remote branch
semantic_limits: The canonical operator recovery remains clean-tree and fail-closed; it does not conceal local changes

candidates.name: Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs
verified_facts: A concurrency group can limit overlapping workflow or job execution
cancel-in-progress can cancel an older in-progress run in the same group
semantic_limits: GitHub Actions concurrency does not control the external Windows F-host persistent daemon

candidates.name: REST API endpoints for workflow runs
verified_facts: The workflow-runs API exposes run status and conclusion and supports cancellation or re-run operations
Run metadata can distinguish queued, in-progress and completed executions
semantic_limits: Repository workflow status is separate from F-host process and heartbeat evidence

candidates.name: REST API endpoints for workflow jobs
verified_facts: The jobs API exposes job status, conclusion, timestamps, runner identity and step summaries
Job evidence can identify repository-side stalls independently of the external F-host
semantic_limits: A successful hosted job cannot substitute for guarded execution on the named F-host
